Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for taking part in our vendor RFP. A few follow-ups from the security and procurement teams:

1) We need an explicit attestation that production data for EU customers will remain resident in EU regions (site-of-record) and a description of activation criteria for any temporary cross-border processing (e.g., failover to us-west). 3) Please provide a network/data flow diagram showing ingress/egress points and any cached/ephemeral KV stores.

Deadline: we need an evidence package by COB 2027-06-14 to include in our compliance pack.

Quick internal notes / proposed evidence items — please treat this as draft:

1) Attestation text (short):
   - "Redwood Inference attests that, for customers who contract for EU residency, production customer data at rest and in transit will remain within designated EU regions and will be served from EU-hosted inference capacity (site-of-record). Temporary cross-border processing (failover) will only occur under defined activation conditions and for a limited duration not exceeding 72 hours unless otherwise mutually agreed). Redwood will notify the customer and provide an incident report within 2 hours of activation and a detailed root cause within 72 hours."

2) Activation criteria (operational triggers):
   - Regional outage exceeding 5 minutes affecting >20% of customer p99 requests
   - Scheduled maintenance where EU capacity has been proactively exhausted and customer-approved burst to other regions is in place
   - Critical security incident requiring evacuation of a region as per our incident response policy

3) Max allowed duration: default 72 hours (extendable only with explicit customer authorization).

4) Staging/non-prod telemetry:
   - We maintain separate telemetry for staging. By default, any telemetry that could include PII is routed to EU telemetry pipelines when the tenant is EU-resident. If a customer uploads real test data, they must opt the tenant into EU-bound staging; otherwise, staging uses synthetic/test-only masking. On-demand purge is supported; we will provide an authenticated deletion endpoint and confirm deletion within 24 hours.

5) Network/data flow diagram: attached (network_flow_diagram.png) with labeled ingress/egress, KV caches and short TTLs, and border proxies.

6) SOC2 excerpt: attached (soc2_sc4_excerpt.pdf) showing controls for logical separation and monitoring.

I attached a draft attestation (rfi_attestation_v1.pdf). Rishi — can you sign off on the wording and I'll add the legal header? Ben — can you confirm the notification SLA wording for the SOW (2 hours for activation notice)?

Laura Bennett
VP, Cloud Operations — Redwood Inference

Anna / GlobalFin team — attaching our evidence bundle for Q12–Q14. Summary answers below and attachments included.

Summary (production residency and failover):
- Site-of-record: Redwood will host and serve production traffic for contracted EU customers from EU regions only; production data at rest/in-transit is retained in EU-hosted infrastructure unless explicit written consent is provided to allow temporary cross-border processing.
- Activation conditions for temporary cross-border processing: regional outage >5 minutes impacting >20% p99 requests, scheduled exhaustion of EU capacity with pre-approved bursts, or critical security incidents requiring evacuation.
- Max default cross-border duration: 72 hours. Extensions require customer authorization.
- Notification SLA: initial activation notice within 2 hours; incident report within 24 hours; detailed RCA within 72 hours.

Staging / pre-prod telemetry:
- By default, staging telemetry for EU-tenants is routed to EU telemetry pipelines. If a customer uploads real PII to staging, they must explicitly enable EU-bound staging for that tenant; otherwise telemetry is masked/synthetic. On-demand deletion endpoint available; confirmation of purge within 24 hours.

Attachments included:
- rfi_attestation_v1.pdf (formal attestation text — suitable for inclusion in your compliance pack)
- network_flow_diagram.png (topology with labeled ingress/egress, ephemeral caches, and border proxies)
- soc2_sc4_excerpt.pdf (SOC2 control excerpt demonstrating logical separation and monitoring)
